pr.title: Remove coroutine info when building coroutine drop body
pr.description: Coroutine drop shims are not themselves coroutines, so erase the "`coroutine`" field from the body so that helper fns like `yield_ty` and `coroutine_kind` properly return `None` for the drop shim.
pr.author: compiler-errors

analysis.originalLogic: In `create_coroutine_drop_shim`, the pass cloned the coroutine MIR body and then only adjusted the ABI-related argument count: `let mut body = body.clone();` followed by `body.arg_count = 1; // make sure the resume argument is not included here`. The clone also retained the source body's `coroutine: Option<Box<CoroutineInfo>>`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Constructing the synthetic coroutine drop shim by clone-and-adjust-arg-count while retaining `body.coroutine` made a non-coroutine drop body carry coroutine metadata. As the PR description states, coroutine drop shims “are not themselves coroutines,” so helper queries such as `yield_ty` and `coroutine_kind` could treat the drop shim as a coroutine instead of returning `None`. The historical fix erases the field with `let _ = body.coroutine.take();` before setting `body.arg_count = 1`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by the `StateTransform` pass for Rust coroutines, specifically the body built by `create_coroutine_drop_shim` for a coroutine that needs drop cleanup. A representative input has a coroutine with a drop-requiring value live across a suspend point, as in the changed `tests/mir-opt/coroutine_drop_cleanup` expectations. The differential input domain is the same coroutine body under two transformations: clone retaining `coroutine` metadata versus clone with `coroutine.take()` before building the drop shim.
analysis.summary: When `StateTransform` builds a coroutine drop shim, the shim is a synthetic non-coroutine body even though it is cloned from a coroutine. Dropping only `arg_count` without clearing `body.coroutine` leaves stale coroutine metadata, causing coroutine helper queries to misclassify the shim. The fix removes `body.coroutine` with `take()` before adjusting the argument count.
analysis.trigger: Building a coroutine drop shim in `create_coroutine_drop_shim` from a coroutine body whose `body.coroutine` is `Some`, especially when the coroutine has state needing cleanup/drop across a suspend point.
preconditions: The source MIR body is a coroutine lowered through `StateTransform` and carries `Some(CoroutineInfo)`.
The pass constructs the coroutine drop shim by cloning that body.
The shim is intended to be a `drop_in_place`-style synthetic body, not a coroutine body.
Changing only `arg_count` does not remove the `coroutine` field or its helpers' observable metadata.
pitfalls: Adjusting `arg_count` alone is insufficient because `body.coroutine` remains populated.
Synthetic MIR bodies derived from coroutine bodies should not automatically retain coroutine metadata; the PR warns this also applies to promoted consts and other synthetic bodies.
Do not infer that the drop shim should keep `yield_ty`, `resume_ty`, or `coroutine_layout` merely because it was cloned from a coroutine.
The test expectation removal of the `coroutine_layout` annotation is evidence about drop-shim metadata, not evidence that the drop control flow itself changed.
analysis.testStrategy: Add or inspect a MIR-opt regression test using a coroutine that stores a drop-requiring local such as `String` across a suspend point (`tests/mir-opt/coroutine_drop_cleanup.rs`). Check the generated `coroutine_drop` shim for the absence of coroutine metadata, matching the updated `.mir` expectations where the `/* coroutine_layout = CoroutineLayout { ... } */` block is removed. Cover both panic modes shown in the patch: `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind`. Also directly test that `yield_ty` and `coroutine_kind` return `None` when queried on the drop-shim body. No compiler execution or reproduction is claimed here.
